---
title: "City2Graph · Import urban data"
---

::: {.lead}
Overture buildings and places, local GIS files, and GTFS feeds for Burjassot.
Mirrors the [Data Import panel](../../../panels/city2graph/data.qmd).
:::

To align downloads with an existing street network, keep an OSMnx network active
and use **From OSMnx** as the area method.

## 1. Define the area

The simplest **Define Area** option is **Place** with
`Burjassot, Valencia, Spain`. **From OSMnx**, **Point**, **Address**, **BBox**
and **Polygon** reuse the OSMnx area fields.

![Defining the Burjassot area in Data Import.](../../../assets/guides/city2graph/01-define-area.png)

## 2. Download Overture features

Toggle the layers you need (**building**, **segment**, **place**, **water**,
**land**) and set a **Limit**. **Get as Mesh** brings in footprints; **Get as
Points** creates point nodes directly.

![Selecting Overture layers and downloading.](../../../assets/guides/city2graph/01-overture.png)

## 3. Convert to centroids

Reduces polygon footprints to one point each, which is the node representation
proximity graphs expect.

![Converting building footprints to centroids.](../../../assets/guides/city2graph/01-centroids.png)

## 4. Load a local file

**Load File** takes a GeoPackage, Shapefile or GeoJSON of your own zones or
features.

![Loading a local GIS file.](../../../assets/guides/city2graph/01-load-file.png)

## 5. Import GTFS

Set **GTFS Path** and press **Import GTFS**, then **Visualize GTFS** to draw
stops and routes. A São Paulo feed ships under `examples/GTFS/`.

![Importing and visualizing a GTFS feed.](../../../assets/guides/city2graph/01-gtfs.png)
